The defectors, who also included the NDC treasurer, Mannir Umar, ward secretaries, women and youth leaders, as well as members of the Kwankwasiyya movement , formally announced their decision during a visit to Bichi at the lawmaker’s office.
The five ward chairmen represented Waire, Danzabuwa, Kaukau, Muntsira and Bichi wards.
Speaking on behalf of the defectors, the Chairman of the Forum and Danzabuwa Ward Chairman, Abdulkadir Lawan, said their decision to join the APC was influenced by Bichi’s developmental projects and empowerment programmes.
Lawan said he personally benefited from the lawmaker’s scholarship initiative, which enabled him to obtain a master’s degree, adding that he was currently pursuing a PhD through the Abubakar Kabir Foundation.
He also cited alleged poor coordination, lack of respect for members and leadership disagreements within the NDC in Kano State as reasons for their departure.
Receiving the defectors, Bichi welcomed them into the APC, expressing appreciation for their confidence in his leadership and describing their decision as a boost to the party’s grassroots mobilisation.
The lawmaker highlighted some of his interventions in Danzabuwa Ward, including the construction of a primary school, ongoing road projects and provision of boreholes.
He urged party members to remain united and intensify grassroots mobilisation to secure victory for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.
The defection ceremony was attended by the APC member representing Bichi Constituency in the Kano State House of Assembly, Lawan Shehu Bichi; the Director-General of the campaign council, Sani Mukaddas Bichi; the Bichi Local Government Vice Chairman, Babangida Danzabuwa; and the APC State Secretary, Prof. Yusuf Muhammad Sabo.
